title: Drop the mid-depth global layer: WINDOW_PATTERN "SSSL" -> "SSSS"
description: One character in the hyperparameter block: WINDOW_PATTERN "SSSL" -> "SSSS", keeping window_sizes[-1] = long, so layers 0-6 use window 512 and only the final layer is global 2048 (baseline had globals at layers 3 and 7). val_bpb 0.989833 at 482.9M tokens / 1842 steps / MFU 34.08% / 45.0GB / queued_s 963; FLOPs/token 220.2M -> 210.8M as predicted.
reflection:
A null, and the reason is the useful part. Control is a2's r02 pair at SSSL/512 (0.989668 @ 486.5M, 0.989981 @ 486.3M; mean 0.989825, spread 0.0003); my file differs by one character. Raw delta +0.000008 = zero. Token-corrected with the within-cluster slope (-0.000128/1M) the residual is -0.00044 (~0.7 sd), i.e. at most a hint that removing the layer-3 global span helps quality, nothing defensible.

The measurement that changes planning: attention FLOPs have stopped converting into tokens. Arithmetic fell 4.3% (220.2M -> 210.8M per token) and tokens went DOWN, 486.4M -> 482.9M, because MFU fell 35.89% -> 34.08%. a2 saw 7.9% FLOPs buy only +2.5% tokens at 1024->512; at 512->fewer-long-layers the conversion is now negative. We are kernel/launch-overhead bound, not attention-arithmetic bound, so no further attention-FLOP cut (shorter windows, fewer long layers, cheaper patterns) should be budgeted as buying tokens. a2's -0.002 quality residual at 1024->512 does not extend: the cross-document-contamination story predicted a further gain from deleting a global layer and the data shows ~0.

So the window axis is closed at 6S+2L/512: the remaining 14 runs should go to axes nobody has measured - DEPTH/ASPECT_RATIO shape, WARMDOWN_RATIO, MLP ratio, number of value-embedding tables - and, given we are overhead-bound at 34% MFU, to anything that raises MFU rather than lowers FLOPs.
